page: Amazon Web Services x2idn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring the x86_64 architecture, configured with 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. The instance includes 1536 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an exceptionally high 16:1 memory-to-core ratio. High-speed local scratch space is bundled via 2850 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network performance is rated at 75 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel execution and high data throughput. Multi-core performance across stress-ng (92,904.33) and Geekbench (18,074.0) ranks in the top 25%, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 76,040.07 and top-tier PassMark encryption performance (87,174.88). Its memory subsystem delivers strong large-block read bandwidth at 326.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 137.6 GB/sec. This translates to high operational throughput in caching layers, reaching 87.7 million Redis SET operations per second and strong PassMark database scores.

Single-threaded execution remains average across benchmarks, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 1,665.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,892.88. Large-model CPU-based LLM generation presents a bottleneck, testing in the bottom 25% for 70B models at 2.76 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated matrix acceleration engines or GPUs. From an efficiency perspective, the platform yields substantial value when consolidated around large datasets requiring rapid memory access, high network ingress/egress, and high local I/O.

AWS x2idn.24xlarge is best suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large in-memory databases like SAP HANA or Redis clusters, real-time big data analytics engines, relational database instances, and network-intensive data processing pipelines.
